# Setup and Data Import
#Loading appropriate packages
```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(EnvStats)
library(tidyr)
library(stats)
library(jtools)
library(effsize)
library(tinytex)
library(ICC)

```

#Organizing Dataframes for Experiment 1
```{r}
#Behavioral Experiment 1 Data Frame
dfexp1<- read.csv("C:/Users/Wallace/Desktop/Jeremy and Ruth Research/RepAggNeuroFinalCode/Spool et al 2026 datasheet experiment 1.csv")

#Behavioral Experiment 1 Data Frame Filter Mirror treatment only
dfexp1mirror<-dfexp1 %>% 
  filter(treatment == "mirror")

#Behavioral Experiment 1 Data Frame Filter Control treatment only
dfexp1control<-dfexp1 %>% 
  filter(treatment == "none")

#Behavioral Experiment 1 Pulling Monday Average Gill Flaring
mondaygillflareexp1mirror<-dfexp1mirror%>% 
  select(monday_average_startflare_prop)
mondaygillflareexp1mirror$experiment<-"behavioral_experiment_1"
colnames(mondaygillflareexp1mirror) <- c("GF","experiment")

#Behavioral Experiment 1 Pulling Gill Flaring For All 3 Mondays aka days 1, 8, and 15 (Mirror and Control treatments included)
dfexp1day1<-dfexp1 %>% 
  gather(key = "day", value = "startflare_prop", monday1_startflare_prop,monday2_startflare_prop,monday3_startflare_prop)
dfexp1day1<-dfexp1day1 %>% 
  select(day, social_treatment, startflare_prop)

#Behavioral Experiment 1 Pulling Gill Flaring For All 3 Thursdays aka days 4, 11, and 18 (Mirror and Control treatments included)
dfexp1day18<-dfexp1 %>% 
  gather(key = "day", value = "startflare_prop", thursday1_startflare_prop,thursday2_startflare_prop,thursday3_startflare_prop)
dfexp1day18<-dfexp1day18 %>% 
  select(day, social_treatment, startflare_prop)

#Behavioral Experiment 1 Comparing Day 1 and Day 18
dffirstlast<-rbind(dfexp1day1, dfexp1day18)
dffirstlast<-dffirstlast %>% filter(day == "monday1_startflare_prop"|day == "thursday3_startflare_prop")

#Behavioral Experiment 1 Comparing Day 1 and Day 18 Control ONLY
dffirstlastcontrol<-dffirstlast %>%
  filter(social_treatment == "none")

#Behavioral Experiment 1 Comparing Day 1 and Day 18 Mirror ONLY
dffirstlastmirror<-dffirstlast %>%
  filter(social_treatment == "mirror")


```

#Organizing Dataframes for Experiment 2
```{r}

#Behavioral Experiment 2 Data Frame
dfexp2<-read.csv("C:/Users/Wallace/Desktop/Jeremy and Ruth Research/RepAggNeuroFinalCode/Spool et al 2026 datasheet experiment 2.csv", na.string = c("", "NA"))

#Organization so plotting has correct order for treatment groups and weeks
dfexp2$treatment = factor(dfexp2$treatment, levels = c("control", "mirror"))
dfexp2$week = factor(dfexp2$week, levels = c("one", "two", "three"))

#Behavioral Experiment 2 Data Frame Filtered Just Mirror treatment
dfexp2mirror<-dfexp2 %>% 
  filter(treatment == "mirror")

#New Data Frame For Experiment 2 Mirror Group ONLY specification so the figure orders days numerically instead of alphabetically 
desired_order = c("one", "two", "three")
dfexp2mirror$week = 
  factor(dfexp2mirror$week, levels = desired_order, ordered = TRUE)

#Behavioral Experiment 2 Data Frame Filtered Just Control treatment
dfexp2control<-dfexp2 %>% 
  filter(treatment == "control")

#Behavioral Experiment 2 Pulling Average Total Gill Flaring
gillflaravgexp2mirror<-dfexp2mirror%>% 
  select(gillflaring_total_average)
gillflaravgexp2mirror$experiment<-"behavioral_experiment_2"
colnames(gillflaravgexp2mirror) <- c("GF","experiment")

#Data Frame to check consistency across behavioral experiment 1 and 2 

#Note that both sets of data are averaged across 3 days of behavior, the only difference is exp1 has the 3 days each separated by one week (Monday 1/2/3), whereas exp2 3 days in a row

behav12check<-bind_rows(mondaygillflareexp1mirror,gillflaravgexp2mirror)

```


# Experiment 1 Behavior
```{r}
#New DataFrame with Week 1 Monday (Day 1) Gill Flaring and Treatment Group
dfexp1mondayflare<-dfexp1day1 %>% 
  filter(day == "monday1_startflare_prop")

#Shapiro Test is not significant indicating that the data is normally distributed.Therefore, a T test is used instead of a Wilcox test
shapiro.test(dfexp1mondayflare$startflare_prop) 

#T Test is significant indicating a significant difference in Day 1 gill flaring between treatment groups (mirror vs control)
t.test(startflare_prop ~ social_treatment, data = dfexp1mondayflare)
cohen.d(startflare_prop ~ social_treatment, data = dfexp1mondayflare)


#Treatment Assessment for Day 18, the final social assay of experiment 1

#New DataFrame with Week 3 Thursday (Day 18) Gill Flaring and Treatment Group
dfexp1thursdayflare<-dfexp1day18 %>% 
  filter(day == "thursday3_startflare_prop")

#Shapiro Test is significant indicating that the data is NOT normally distributed.Therefore, a Kruskal-Wallis/Wilcox is used instead of an Anova/T-test
shapiro.test(dfexp1thursdayflare$startflare_prop)

#Wilcox Test is significant indicating a significant difference in Day 18 gill flaring between treatment groups (mirror vs control)
wilcox.test(startflare_prop ~ social_treatment, data = dfexp1thursdayflare)
cohen.d(startflare_prop ~ social_treatment, data = dfexp1thursdayflare)


#Treatment Day 1 vs Day 18

#Shapiro Test is significant meaning the data is NOT normally distributed. A Wilcox test is used instead of T test
shapiro.test(dffirstlast$startflare_prop)

#Wilcox was not significant meaning there is no difference between gill flaring on first and last day for ALL participants
wilcox.test(startflare_prop ~ day, data = dffirstlast)

#Wilcox was significant meaning there is a difference between gill flaring on first and last day for control ONLY
wilcox.test(startflare_prop ~ day, data = dffirstlastcontrol)
cohen.d(startflare_prop ~ day, data = dffirstlastcontrol)

#Wilcox was not significant meaning there is no difference between gill flaring on first and last day for mirror ONLY
wilcox.test(startflare_prop ~ day, data = dffirstlastmirror)

```

## Figure 4a
```{r}

p <- ggplot(dffirstlast, aes(x=day, y=startflare_prop)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = social_treatment), lwd=1, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_dotplot(aes(type = social_treatment), binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center", position =    
  position_dodge(width = 0.8), dotsize = 0.7) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  scale_fill_manual(values= c("cadetblue", "coral3"))+
  labs(x="Day", y="% Time Gill Flaring") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("Day 1","Day 18"))
plot(p)
```


```{r}
#Comparison of scototaxis behavior between mirror and control at the beginning and end of the expeirment (aka day 5 first scoto and day 19 last scoto)

#New Data Frame With Behavior Experiment 1 Week 1, Week 2, Week 3 Friday, proportion of time spent on black side of the scototaxis assay
dfexp1scotofriday123<-dfexp1 %>% 
  gather(key = "day", value = "black_prop", friday1_black_prop, friday2_black_prop, friday3_black_prop)
dfexp1scotofriday123<-dfexp1scotofriday123 %>%
  select(day, social_treatment, black_prop)

#Average across all Fridays: general proportion time spent on black side in scototaxis in experiment 1
mean(dfexp1scotofriday123$black_prop)

#New Data Frame For Just Friday Week 1, proportion of time spent on black side and treatment group
dfexp1scotofriday1<-dfexp1scotofriday123 %>% 
  filter(day == "friday1_black_prop") 

#Shapiro Test was NOT significant meaning that the data IS normally distributed and an anova/t-test can be used
shapiro.test(dfexp1scotofriday1$black_prop)

#T-test showed no significant difference between treatment groups and proportion of time spent on black side of tank on Friday Week 1
t.test(black_prop ~social_treatment, data = dfexp1scotofriday1)


#New Data Frame For Just Friday Week 3 proportion of time spent on black side and treatment group
dfexp1scotofriday3<-dfexp1scotofriday123 %>%
  filter(day == "friday3_black_prop") 

#Shapiro Test was NOT significant meaning that the data IS normally distributed and an anova/t-test can be used
shapiro.test(dfexp1scotofriday3$black_prop)

#T-test showed no significant difference between treatment groups and proportion of time spent on black side of tank on Friday Week 3
t.test(black_prop ~social_treatment, data = dfexp1scotofriday3)


#New Data Frame For Just Friday 1 and Friday 3, proportion of time spent on black side, and BOTH treatment groups  
dfexp1scotofriday13<-dfexp1scotofriday123 %>% 
  filter(day == "friday1_black_prop"|day == "friday3_black_prop")


#Shapiro Test was NOT significant meaning there was normal distribution between all the Friday's 
shapiro.test(dfexp1scotofriday13$black_prop)

#New Data Frame For Just Friday 1 and Friday 3, proportion of time spent on black side, and mirror ONLY
dfexp1scotofriday13m<-dfexp1scotofriday123 %>% 
  filter(day == "friday1_black_prop"|day == "friday3_black_prop")
dfexp1scotofriday13m<-dfexp1scotofriday13m %>% 
  filter(social_treatment == "mirror")

#T-test showed no significant difference between Friday Week 1 and Friday Week 3 mirror ONLY
t.test(black_prop ~ day, data = dfexp1scotofriday13m)

#New Data Frame For Just Friday 1 and Friday 3, proportion of time spent on black side, and control ONLY
dfexp1scotofriday13c<-dfexp1scotofriday123 %>% 
  filter(day == "friday1_black_prop"|day == "friday3_black_prop")
dfexp1scotofriday13c<-dfexp1scotofriday13c %>% 
  filter(social_treatment == "none")

#T-test showed no significant difference between Friday Week 1 and Friday Week 3 control ONLY
t.test(black_prop ~ day, data = dfexp1scotofriday13c)

```

# Experiment 2 Behavior
```{r}
#average time spent near stimulus (mirror only)
mean(dfexp2mirror$location_total_average)
sd(dfexp2mirror$location_total_average)

#average time spent near stimulus (control only)
mean(dfexp2control$location_total_average)
sd(dfexp2control$location_total_average)

#Shapiro test was significant indicating that the data is NOT normally distributed
shapiro.test(dfexp2$location_total_average)

#Wilcox showed a significant difference in total average location between mirror and control group 
wilcox.test(location_total_average ~ treatment, data = dfexp2)
cohen.d(location_total_average ~ treatment, data = dfexp2)

#now running the difference between total average location between mirror and control group - WEEK 1
dftemp<- dfexp2 %>% filter(week == "one")
wilcox.test(location_total_average ~ treatment, data = dftemp)
cohen.d(location_total_average ~ treatment, data = dftemp)

#now running the difference between total average location between mirror and control group - WEEK 2
dftemp<- dfexp2 %>% filter(week == "two")
wilcox.test(location_total_average ~ treatment, data = dftemp)
cohen.d(location_total_average ~ treatment, data = dftemp)

#now running the difference between total average location between mirror and control group - WEEK 3
dftemp<- dfexp2 %>% filter(week == "three")
wilcox.test(location_total_average ~ treatment, data = dftemp)


#does the control significantly differ from 50%
shapiro.test(dfexp2control$location_total_average)
wilcox.test(dfexp2control$location_total_average, mu = 0.5)
cohen.d(dfexp2control$location_total_average~1, mu = 0.5)

#Gill Flaring Latency Average
mean(dfexp2mirror$gillflaring_latency_average, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(dfexp2mirror$gillflaring_latency_average, na.rm = TRUE)

#average bite latency
mean(dfexp2mirror$bite_latency_average, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(dfexp2mirror$bite_latency_average, na.rm = TRUE)


bitemod <- glm(dfexp2mirror$bite_latency_average ~ dfexp2mirror$gillflaring_prior_average)
summ(bitemod)


```

```{r}
#behavior did not change over the three weeks in exp 2

#Kruskal-Wallis showed no significant difference in total average location in mirror group ONLY across weeks
shapiro.test(dfexp2mirror$location_total_average)
kruskal.test(location_total_average ~ week, data = dfexp2mirror)

#Kruskal-Wallis showed no significant difference in total average location in control group ONLY across weeks
shapiro.test(dfexp2control$location_total_average)
kruskal.test(location_total_average ~ week, data = dfexp2control)



#Shapiro Test is NOT significant indicating that the data is normally distributed. An Anova test is used instead of a Kruskal-Wallis Test
shapiro.test(dfexp2mirror$gillflaring_total_average)

#Anova Test showed no significant difference between the average amount of time spent gill flaring each week in the mirror group ONLY
gillflarexp2week123<-aov(gillflaring_total_average ~ week, dfexp2mirror)
summary(gillflarexp2week123)
p_value_aov<-summary(gillflarexp2week123)[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]


#Shapiro test was NOT significant indicating that the data IS normally distributed. An Anova test is used instead of a Kruskal-Wallis
shapiro.test(dfexp2mirror$bite_latency_average)

#Anova Test showed no significant difference between average bite latency across weeks for mirror group ONLY
bitelatencyexp2week123<-aov(bite_latency_average ~ week, dfexp2mirror)
summary(bitelatencyexp2week123)
p_value_aov<-summary(bitelatencyexp2week123)[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]


#Shapiro test was significant indicating that the data is NOT normally distributed. An Kruskal-Wallis test is used instead of an Anova
shapiro.test(dfexp2mirror$gillflaring_latency_average)

#Kruskal-Wallis showed no significant difference between average gill flaring latency across weeks for mirror group ONLY
kruskal.test(gillflaring_latency_average ~ week, data = dfexp2mirror)

#Shapiro test was NOT significant indicating that the data IS normally distributed. An Anova test is used instead of a Kruskal-Wallis
shapiro.test(dfexp2mirror$gillflaring_prior_average)

#Anova Test showed no significant difference in gill flaring prior to first bite across weeks for mirror ONLY
gillflarpriorexp2week123<-aov(gillflaring_prior_average ~ week, dfexp2mirror)
summary(gillflarpriorexp2week123)
p_value_aov<-summary(gillflarpriorexp2week123)[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]


```

```{r}


#GSI
temp<-dfexp2mirror
temp$gsi<-as.numeric(temp$gsi)
mean(temp$gsi, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(temp$gsi, na.rm = TRUE)

#GSI showed no difference between weeks or between mirror/control
mod<-aov(gsi ~ week, temp)
summary(mod)


temp2<-dfexp2
temp2$gsi<-as.numeric(temp2$gsi)
mod<-aov(gsi ~ treatment, temp2)
summary(mod)
p_value_aov<-summary(mod)[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
p_value_aov


#GSI by gill flaring average across 3 days is not significant
gsimod <- glm(temp$gillflaring_total_average ~ temp$gsi)
summ(gsimod)

#GSI by gill flaring latency across 3 days is not significant
gsimod <- glm(temp$gillflaring_latency_average ~ temp$gsi)
summ(gsimod)


#GSI by bite latency across 3 days is not significant
gsimod <- glm(temp$bite_latency_average ~ temp$gsi)
summ(gsimod)

#GSI linear model trend correlation with cortisol, posthoc with a gamma family is significant
gsimod <- lm(temp$cort_level ~ temp$gsi)
summ(gsimod)

gsimod <- glm(temp$cort_level ~ temp$gsi, family = Gamma)
summary(gsimod)
summ(gsimod)


```

# Experiment 2 Immunohistochemistry

```{r}

#All p value statistical tests for PS6 expression (VS DCX tests are separate)


#Mirror vs Control (ALL REGIONS)

#Rostral Vs
shapiro.test(dfexp2$vs_rostral)

t_test<-t.test(vs_rostral ~ treatment, data = dfexp2)
p_value_t<-t_test$p.value
p.adjust(p_value_t, method = "fdr", n = 7)
cohen.d(vs_rostral ~ treatment, data = dfexp2)

#Caudal Vs
shapiro.test(dfexp2$vs_caudal)

t_test<-t.test(vs_caudal ~ treatment, data = dfexp2)
p_value_t<-t_test$p.value
p.adjust(p_value_t, method = "fdr", n = 7)


################################
#Posthoc correlating behavior in just the Vs (mirror group only, all weeks combined)

#total average amount of gill flaring on the final day (DAY 3) does not significantly correlate to Vs expression
```

# Experiment 2 Cortisol
```{r}
#Shapiro test IS significant indicating that the data is NOT normally distributed. A Kruskal-Wallis test is used instead of an Anova. 
shapiro.test(dfexp2mirror$cort_level)

#Kruskal-Wallis showed no significant difference in cortisol levels in mirror ONLY between weeks
kruskal.test(cort_level ~ week, data = dfexp2mirror)

#Wilcox test showed no significant difference between cortisol level and treatment group 
wilcox.test(cort_level ~ treatment, data = dfexp2)

#Linear model showed no significant correlation between cortisol level and gill flaring on the day cortisol levels were taken in mirror group ONLY
cortgill <- lm(dfexp2mirror$cort_level ~ dfexp2mirror$gillflaring_total_day1)
 p_value <- summary(cortgill)$coefficients[8]
 p_value
 
 
```
